title: Pope Leo XIV is not a fan of AI-generated art
key_facts: Pope Leo XIV posted on X on Friday morning (2 Oct 2026) about the difference between human art and art generated by machines.

He wrote that it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce, and that there is an "ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one" between art and what a machine generates from statistical calculation on millions of images made by others.
He wrote that "Algorithms lack the spark of humanity."
The post was part of a call to preserve human art from the encroachment of AI.
TechCrunch notes the Pope gave a more detailed statement on AI in an encyclical letter in May, stressing human dignity in a world of increasing automation.
TechCrunch cites a recent New York Times report that Anthropic has actively lobbied the Vatican to reconsider its position on non-human consciousness, apparently with little success.
quote_evidence: In a post on X Friday morning, Pope Leo XIV detailed the spiritual difference between human-generated art and art that is generated by machines, as part of a call to preserve human art from the encroachment of AI.

why_it_matters_hint: A leading world religious figure has publicly sided with human artists in the debate over AI-generated art.
notes: Short article (about 1,700 characters after removing event adverts). The post itself is quoted directly by TechCrunch; the Anthropic lobbying claim is TechCrunch relaying a New York Times report and is not checked here.
